mainTopic: רבי פנחס בן יאיר's donkey and his meeting with רבי, the tithing of animal food, the greatness of צדיקים after death, and teachings of רבי חנינא about mules, כשפים and Heavenly decrees
overview: The גמרא finishes the story of רבי פנחס בן יאיר's donkey, which would not eat barley until it was tithed. It then asks whether animal food needs tithing at all, and רבי יוחנן answers that the exemption only applies to food bought for an animal from the start. The story goes on: רבי invites רבי פנחס בן יאיר to eat with him. He accepts, explaining he only avoids hosts who cannot afford guests or do not truly want them. When he returns from his מצוה, he sees dangerous white mules at רבי's door and refuses to enter. Every solution רבי offers runs into an איסור, until a mountain rises between them and רבי says צדיקים are even greater after death. The גמרא proves this from אלישע's bones and discusses how אליהו's double-portion blessing was fulfilled. It then brings teachings about white mules, about כשפים having no power against ה׳, and about small injuries being decreed in Heaven. It ends by describing how רבי פנחס בן יאיר never benefited from anyone else's food.

steps.title: The donkey refuses the barley until it is tithed
steps.stepSummary: The hosts clean the barley in two different ways, but the donkey still won't eat. Once they tithe it, the donkey eats.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sifted the barley, and the donkey didn't eat. They picked out the chaff by hand, and it still didn't eat. רבי פנחס בן יאיר said to them: 'Maybe it isn't tithed?' They tithed it, and the donkey ate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the story of רבי פנחס בן יאיר's donkey. The hosts first think the barley is dirty, but the real problem is that it was never tithed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hosts try two physical fixes, sifting and hand-picking, and neither works. Only the halachic fix, separating מעשרות, makes the donkey eat. The point is that the animal of a צדיק is kept from eating forbidden food.

keyTerms.meaning: They sifted or beat it (the barley), to clean it
They picked through it by hand to remove the chaff

phrases.english: They sifted it, but it did not eat.
phrases.notes: 'They' are the hosts at the inn, and 'it' is רבי פנחס בן יאיר's donkey eating their barley.

phrases.english: They cleaned it by hand, but it did not eat.
He said to them: Perhaps it is not tithed?
They tithed it, and it ate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the donkey story from the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The donkey of a צדיק refused untithed barley and ate only once it was tithed.

steps.title: רבי פנחס בן יאיר rebukes his hosts
steps.stepSummary: רבי פנחס בן יאיר criticizes the hosts for feeding טבלים to an animal that is on its way to do a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: 'This poor animal is going to do the will of its Creator, and you are feeding it untithed food!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פנחס בן יאיר scolds the hosts for giving his donkey untithed food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His complaint assumes that even food given to an animal should be tithed. That assumption sets up the next step, where the גמרא asks whether animal food really needs tithing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Poor thing; an expression of pity
Produce whose תרומות and מעשרות have not been separated; forbidden to eat

phrases.english: He said: This poor creature
is going to do the will of its Maker,
and you are feeding it untithed produce!

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲנִיָּיה זוֹ הוֹלֶכֶת לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן קוֹנָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the lesson of the donkey's behavior.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Untithed produce should not be fed even to an animal, and certainly not to one on its way to do a מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: His words imply that animal food needs tithing, which the גמרא is about to question.

steps.title: Does animal food need tithing? A משנה says it is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the assumption that the barley needed tithing. A משנה in דמאי exempts food bought for an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is one obligated to tithe? Don't we learn: One who buys produce for planting or for an animal, flour for working hides, oil for a lamp, or oil to grease vessels is exempt from דמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the story to ask a halachic question. Why did the barley need tithing, if a משנה says food bought for animals is exempt from דמאי?
steps.deeperAnalysis: דמאי is produce bought from an עם הארץ who may not have tithed it. The משנה lists purchases that are not for human eating, including animal feed, and exempts them. If animal feed is exempt, then the hosts did nothing wrong and the rebuke seems unjustified.

keyTerms.meaning: And is one obligated? This introduces a challenge.
Produce bought from an עם הארץ, where it is doubtful whether it was tithed

phrases.english: And is one obligated?
But didn't we learn: One who buys for seed or for an animal,
or flour for hides, or oil for a lamp,
or oil to smear on vessels
is exempt from דמאי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the halachic assumption behind רבי פנחס בן יאיר's rebuke.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that grain fed to an animal must be tithed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה explicitly exempts דמאי bought for an animal, so the barley needed no tithing.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not doubting the story. It is asking how the halacha fits the story.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the exemption applies only if it was bought for the animal from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limits the משנה to food bought for an animal from the start. Food bought for people and later switched to an animal still needs tithing.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it was said about that משנה, רבי יוחנן said: They taught this only when he bought it for an animal from the start. But if he bought it for people and then changed his mind and decided to use it for an animal, he must tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with רבי יוחנן's explanation of the משנה, which narrows the exemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is the purpose at the time of buying. The hosts bought the barley as human food and only later gave it to the donkey, so it still needed tithing. This means the rebuke was justified.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in a case of; a phrase that limits a ruling
From the start; at the time of purchase

phrases.english: There, it was already said about it,
Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלְּקָחָן מִתְּחִלָּה לִבְהֵמָה,
phrases.english: They taught this only where he bought them from the start for an animal,
but if he bought them from the start for a person
and changed his mind about them, deciding to use them for an animal,
he is obligated to tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the משנה in דמאי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the משנה (לא שנו אלא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All produce given to an animal is exempt from דמאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only produce bought for an animal from the start is exempt. Produce bought for people and later given to an animal must be tithed.
steps.whatToRemember: For דמאי, the purpose at the time of purchase decides. Food bought for people and later switched to an animal still needs tithing.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that food bought to eat and later switched to an animal may not be fed to any animal until it is tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: One who buys produce from the market to eat and then decides to give it to an animal may not put it in front of his own animal or his friend's animal unless he tithed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states the case of changing one's mind outright and requires tithing. It adds that this applies even to someone else's animal, so the obligation stays with the food itself.

keyTerms.meaning: For eating, meaning for human consumption

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: הַלּוֹקֵחַ פֵּירוֹת מִן הַשּׁוּק לַאֲכִילָה
phrases.english: And it was taught: One who buys produce from the market for eating
and changed his mind about it, deciding to use it for an animal,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִתֵּן לֹא לִפְנֵי בְּהֶמְתּוֹ
phrases.english: should not put it in front of his own animal
nor in front of his friend's animal
unless he tithed it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: הַלּוֹקֵחַ פֵּירוֹת מִן הַשּׁוּק לַאֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that food bought for people and then switched to an animal must be tithed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that forbids feeding such produce to any animal until it is tithed.
steps.confusionAlert: Here וְהָתַנְיָא supports the previous answer. It is not a new challenge, even though the same word often introduces one.

steps.title: רבי invites רבי פנחס בן יאיר to eat with him
steps.stepSummary: The story resumes. רבי goes out to greet רבי פנחס בן יאיר, invites him to a meal, and is delighted when he accepts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי heard about it and went out to greet him. He said to him: 'Would you like to eat with me?' He said: 'Yes.' רבי's face lit up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story. רבי יהודה הנשיא invites רבי פנחס בן יאיר to eat with him and is overjoyed when he agrees, which sets up what happens next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי פנחס בן יאיר was known for not eating at other people's tables, so his 'yes' made רבי very happy. The next step explains why he usually refused and why he agreed this time.

keyTerms.meaning: To dine or eat a meal
His face lit up with joy

phrases.english: Rabbi heard, and went out to greet him.
He said to him: Do you want to eat with me?
He said to him: Yes.
Rabbi's face lit up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the story after the halachic side discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי invites רבי פנחס בן יאיר to eat with him, and he accepts.

steps.title: Why he usually refuses invitations, and why he accepts רבי's
steps.stepSummary: רבי פנחס בן יאיר explains that he has no vow against benefiting from Jews. He avoids invitations because hosts either cannot afford guests or do not truly want them. רבי both wants to host and can afford it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you think I am forbidden by a vow from benefiting from Jews? The Jewish people are holy. But some people want to host and cannot afford it, and some can afford it and do not want to. About that second kind the פסוק says: 'Do not eat the bread of a stingy person... "Eat and drink," he says to you, but his heart is not with you.' You, however, want to host, and you can afford it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פנחס בן יאיר answers רבי's delight. He explains that his habit of refusing meals is not because of a vow, and he says why he is willing to accept this time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי might have thought that רבי פנחס בן יאיר had a נדר against getting הנאה from other Jews. He rejects that idea and gives the real reason. A good meal needs both a host who wants to give and a host who is able to give. רבי has both, so accepting his invitation causes no burden and no hidden resentment.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden by a vow from getting any benefit
Someone with an 'evil eye': stingy and resentful about giving
Do you think? / Are you under the impression?

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a guest's sensitivity. One should not eat at the expense of a host who cannot afford it or who gives grudgingly.

phrases.english: He said to him: Do you think
that I am forbidden by a vow from benefiting from Jews?
The Jewish people are holy.
There is one who wants to host but does not have the means,
and there is one who has the means but does not want to,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״אַל תִּלְחַם אֶת לֶחֶם רַע עָיִן
phrases.english: and it is written: "Do not eat the bread of one with an evil eye,
and do not desire his delicacies,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי כְּמוֹ שָׁעַר בְּנַפְשׁוֹ כֶּן הוּא
phrases.english: for as he calculates within himself, so is he;
'Eat and drink,' he will say to you,
but his heart is not with you."
But you want to, and you have the means.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: כִּמְדוּמֶּה אַתָּה שֶׁמּוּדָּר הֲנָאָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל אֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why he accepted the invitation that רבי was so happy about in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He has no vow. He avoids hosts who cannot afford guests or who give grudgingly, but רבי is willing and able.

steps.title: He postpones the meal until after his מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי פנחס בן יאיר says he is in a hurry because he is busy with a מצוה. He promises to come to רבי on his way back.
steps.simpleTranslation: But right now I am in a hurry, because I am busy with a מצוה. When I come back, I will come in to you.
steps.whatsHappening: He accepts the invitation but delays it. This sets up the next part of the story, when he comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His acceptance is real, but the מצוה comes first. Because the meal is pushed to the return trip, the next scene can happen at רבי's door.

keyTerms.meaning: I am rushing, in a hurry
I am busy with, putting effort into

phrases.english: However, right now I am in a hurry,
because I am busy with a matter of a מצוה;
when I come back,
I will come in to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After accepting, he explains that the meal must wait until his מצוה is done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מצוה comes first. He will eat with רבי on his return.

steps.title: He sees white mules and refuses to eat there
steps.stepSummary: On his way back, רבי פנחס בן יאיר enters by a door where white mules are standing. He declares that he cannot eat in a house that holds such deadly danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came back, he happened to enter through the doorway where white mules were standing. He said: The Angel of Death is in this man's house, and I should eat with him?
steps.whatsHappening: The story takes a twist. Just as the promised meal is about to happen, רבי פנחס בן יאיר sees something dangerous and refuses to stay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: White mules were considered deadly animals, so he calls them the מלאך המות. He objects to eating in a house where the owner keeps something so dangerous.

phrases.english: When he came back,
he happened to enter through that doorway
where white mules were standing.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת בְּבֵיתוֹ שֶׁל זֶה
phrases.english: He said: The Angel of Death is in this man's house,
and I should eat with him?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא, אִיתְרְמִי עָל בְּהָהוּא פִּיתְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: He returns as promised in step 8 but finds a reason not to go in.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He will not dine in a house where deadly animals are kept.

steps.title: רבי offers to sell the mules
steps.stepSummary: רבי hears the objection, goes out to meet רבי פנחס בן יאיר, and offers to sell the mules.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי heard and went out to meet him. He said to him: I will sell them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי tries to fix the problem so his guest will come in. This sets up רבי פנחס בן יאיר's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's idea is simple: if the danger leaves my house, the objection is gone. He does not yet consider what happens to whoever buys them.

phrases.english: רבי heard and went out to meet him.
He said to him: I will sell them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי proposes a solution to the objection raised in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי offers to remove the danger by selling the mules.

steps.title: Selling them would be לפני עור
steps.stepSummary: רבי פנחס בן יאיר rejects the offer. Selling a dangerous animal to someone else breaks the איסור of placing a stumbling block before the blind.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Do not place a stumbling block before the blind.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פנחס בן יאיר pushes back on רבי's solution with a פסוק. Selling the danger to someone else is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting rid of the mules by selling them only moves the danger onto the buyer. That counts as putting a מכשול in front of another person, so the fix itself is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The איסור of putting a stumbling block before the blind, meaning causing another person harm or sin
A stumbling block, an obstacle that causes someone to fall

steps.confusionAlert: He is not saying רבי's offer was harmless. A problem you remove from yourself by passing it to someone else is still a problem you caused.
steps.whyThisMatters: It extends לפני עור to selling a dangerous item. You may not hand off a danger to another Jew.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״וְלִפְנֵי עִוֵּר לֹא תִתֵּן מִכְשֹׁל״.
phrases.english: He said to him: "Do not place a stumbling block before the blind."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְלִפְנֵי עִוֵּר לֹא תִתֵּן מִכְשֹׁל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי's proposed solution from step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea of solving the danger by selling the mules.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Selling simply passes the deadly animals to a buyer, which violates לפני עור.

steps.title: Three more offers, three more rejections
steps.stepSummary: רבי offers to make the mules ownerless, cut their hooves, or kill them. רבי פנחס בן יאיר rejects each idea with a halachic problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי: 'I will make them ownerless.' רבי פנחס בן יאיר: 'You will only increase the damage.' רבי: 'I will cut off their hooves.' רבי פנחס בן יאיר: 'That is causing animals pain.' רבי: 'I will kill them.' רבי פנחס בן יאיר: 'That is wasteful destruction.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי keeps suggesting ways to get rid of the danger, and רבי פנחס בן יאיר shoots down each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making them ownerless is worse, because no owner will hold them back. Cutting their hooves breaks the rule against causing animals pain. Killing them breaks the rule against destroying useful things, so every way out runs into an איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: Causing pain to animals, which is forbidden

phrases.english: I will declare them ownerless,
phrases.notes: Here רבי is speaking. The speakers switch back and forth on every line.

phrases.english: You will increase the damage.
I will cut off their hooves,
phrases.notes: Literally 'I will uproot them'; 'the hooves' is understood.

phrases.english: There is the problem of causing animals pain.
I will kill them,
There is the איסור of 'do not destroy.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the back-and-forth after the offer to sell the mules was rejected
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Each of רבי's three proposed solutions
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each solution breaks a different halacha: more damage, צער בעלי חיים, or בל תשחית

steps.title: A mountain separates them and רבי cries
steps.stepSummary: רבי begs a lot, a mountain miraculously rises between them, and רבי cries that צדיקים must be even greater after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי kept pleading with him, until a mountain rose up between them. רבי cried and said: 'If they are like this in their lifetime, how much more so in their death!'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a miracle that separates the two, and רבי reacts with a statement about צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeing that a צדיק can bring about such a miracle while alive, רבי reasons that after death their power is even greater. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא brings a source for this idea.

phrases.english: He was pleading with him a great deal,
until a mountain rose up between them,
רבי cried and said:
If in their lifetime it is like this,
phrases.notes: 'Their' means צדיקים, righteous people like רבי פנחס בן יאיר.

phrases.english: in their death, how much more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story and draws a lesson from it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדיקים are even greater after their death than during their lives

steps.title: The proof from אלישע's bones
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר חנינא teaches that צדיקים are greater in death, proving it from the dead man revived by touching אלישע's bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חמא בר חנינא said: צדיקים are greater in their death than in their life, as it says: 'As they were burying a man, they saw a raiding band, and they threw the man into אלישע's grave. The man touched אלישע's bones, came back to life, and stood on his feet.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי's words with a teaching and a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after אלישע died, his bones had the power to bring a dead man back to life. That shows a צדיק's power continues and even grows after death.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said:
Righteous people are greater in their death
than in their lifetime,
as it says: 'And it was, as they were burying a man,'
and behold, they saw the raiding band,
and they threw the man into Elisha's grave,
and the man went and touched Elisha's bones,
and he came alive and stood up on his feet.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי's statement with a source
steps.raayaObject: צדיקים are greater after death than in life
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 13:21, the dead man revived by touching אלישע's bones

steps.title: Maybe it was to fulfill אליהו's blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests the miracle happened to complete אליהו's blessing of a double portion, not to show greatness after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But maybe it happened to fulfill אליהו's blessing to אלישע, as it is written: 'Let there be a double portion of your spirit upon me'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the proof by offering a different reason for the miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the miracle was needed to make אלישע's miracles add up to double אליהו's, then it says nothing about צדיקים being greater after death. The proof would fall away.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But maybe it was to fulfill for him
the blessing of Eliyahu,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וִיהִי נָא פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּרוּחֲךָ אֵלָי״?
phrases.english: as it is written: 'Please let there be a double portion of your spirit upon me'?
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 2:9. He means אלישע had to do double what אליהו did, so this revival would complete the count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 14
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The miracle can be explained by the need to fulfill אליהו's blessing, so it does not prove greatness after death

steps.title: The man did not really return to life
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the revived man stood up but did not go home, so this could not count toward אלישע's double portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, how does that fit with what a ברייתא teaches: 'He stood on his feet, but he did not go to his home'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back against רב פפא's challenge using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this miracle were meant to fulfill the blessing, it should have been a full revival. The ברייתא says the man never went home, which shows it was not a lasting return to life. So the miracle came from the power of the צדיק's bones, and the proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this what (used here as a challenge)

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
is that what was taught in a ברייתא:
He stood on his feet,
but he did not go to his home!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הָכִי, הַיְינוּ דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge and saves the proof
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a ברייתא showing the case does not fit the challenger's explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The revival completed אליהו's double-portion blessing
steps.terutzMaskana: It was not a full revival, so it could not fulfill the blessing; it shows the power of a צדיק after death

steps.title: So how was the blessing fulfilled?
steps.stepSummary: If this revival does not count, the גמרא asks how אליהו's blessing of a double portion came true.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, in what way was the blessing fulfilled?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the revival doesn't count, the גמרא asks a follow-up question. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer leaves a gap: אלישע seems to be missing one revival to reach double אליהו's. The גמרא wants to know what filled that gap.

phrases.english: But then, in what way was it fulfilled?
phrases.notes: 'It' means אליהו's blessing of a double portion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from אביי's answer, which left the blessing unexplained
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which act of אלישע fulfilled the double-portion blessing

steps.title: Healing נעמן's צרעת counted as reviving the dead
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the blessing was fulfilled when אלישע healed נעמן's צרעת, since a מצורע is considered like a dead person.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: It was fulfilled when he healed נעמן's צרעת, because צרעת is considered like death, as it says: 'Please, let her not be like a dead person.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with רבי יוחנן's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצורע is treated like a dead person, as the פסוק about מרים shows. So healing נעמן counted as bringing someone back to life, which gave אלישע his double portion.

keyTerms.meaning: A skin affliction described in the תורה
Equal to, considered the same as

steps.whatToRemember: צדיקים are greater after death than in life, as seen from אלישע's bones. אליהו's double-portion blessing was fulfilled through healing נעמן, because a מצורע is considered like a dead person.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said:
That he healed Naaman's tzaraas,
which is considered the same as death,
as it says: 'Please, let her not be like a dead person.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 12:12, said about מרים when she had צרעת.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שֶׁרִיפֵּא צָרַעַת נַעֲמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blessing was fulfilled through healing נעמן, since a מצורע counts as dead

steps.title: Why mules are called ימים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains that mules are called ימים because people are terrified of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Why are they called 'ימים'? Because fear of them is cast over all creatures.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about mules, linked to the white mules mentioned earlier on the דף. רבי יהושע בן לוי explains their name, ימים, as coming from the word for fear, אימה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the name ימים as a hint to אימתם, 'their terror'. The point is that these animals are truly dangerous. The next step brings support for this claim.

keyTerms.meaning: A name for mules, based on a פסוק in בראשית
Their terror, the fear they cause

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Why are they called 'yemim'?
phrases.notes: The word comes from בראשית 36:24, which the גמרא reads as talking about mules.

phrases.english: Because their terror is cast over all creatures,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about mules, linked to the white mules discussed earlier on the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mules are called ימים because people are terrified of them.

steps.title: Nobody survives a white mule's wound
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא supports the idea by saying no one ever asked him about a white mule's wound and survived.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חנינא said: In all my days, no person ever asked me about a wound from a white mule and lived.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי יהושע בן לוי by quoting רבי חנינא. He says a wound from a white mule always kills.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows why mules cause such fear: their wounds are deadly. But the claim is very strong, and the next steps will test it against what people actually see.

keyTerms.meaning: A wound from a white mule

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chanina said:
In all my days, no person asked me
about a wound from a white mule and lived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives support for the claim that mules are terrifying.
steps.raayaObject: That mules are frightening and dangerous.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חנינא's experience that no one with a white mule wound survived.

steps.title: But people do survive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that we see people survive white mule wounds.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we see that people do survive!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא's statement using what people actually see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wounds from white mules always kill, how come we see people who lived? The claim seems too strong.

phrases.english: But we see that they survive!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי חנינא's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's claim that no one survives a white mule wound.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Real life shows survivors, so the statement cannot be true as stated.

steps.title: Read it as: the wound never heals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the reading: the wound does not heal, even if the person lives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'and it healed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading one word differently. רבי חנינא meant the wound never heals, not that the person dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of וחיה ('and he lived'), read וחיית ('and it healed'). So the person may live, but the wound stays.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead, read it this way

phrases.english: Say: 'and it healed,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא meant the person dies.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant the wound never heals.

steps.title: But the wounds do heal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects again: we see these wounds heal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we see that they heal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading, again using what people see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the softer reading seems wrong, because white mule wounds are seen to heal.

phrases.english: But we see that they heal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the wound never heals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Real life shows these wounds healing.

steps.title: Only mules with white leg tops
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the case to mules whose legs are white at the top.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about mules whose legs are white at the top.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by limiting which mules רבי חנינא meant. Only a certain kind of white mule causes wounds that never heal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wounds people see healing come from other mules. רבי חנינא's statement is limited to mules white at the top of their legs.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא's statement was narrowed twice: the wound does not heal (not that the person dies), and only from a mule white at the top of its legs.

phrases.english: We are speaking of those whose legs are white at the top.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any white mule's wound never heals.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a mule white at the top of its legs.

steps.title: Even כשפים cannot go against ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא teaches from 'there is none besides Him' that even כשפים have no power.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'There is none besides Him' — רבי חנינא said: and even sorcery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי חנינא. He reads the פסוק 'there is none besides Him' to include כשפים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing has power apart from ה׳, so even כשפים cannot work against His will. A story about רבי חנינא follows to show this.

phrases.english: 'There is none besides Him' —
Rabbi Chanina said: and even sorcery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from רבי חנינא, who was quoted in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even כשפים have no power against ה׳.

steps.title: The woman who tried to bewitch רבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: A woman tried to take dust from under רבי חנינא's feet for כשפים, and he told her it would not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman kept trying to take dust from under רבי חנינא's feet. He said to her: Take it, your plan will not succeed, since it is written 'there is none besides Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing רבי חנינא living by his teaching. He was not afraid of the woman's כשפים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dust from under someone's feet was used for כשפים against him. רבי חנינא let her take it, because he trusted the פסוק that nothing works against ה׳.

phrases.english: There was a certain woman who kept trying

phrases.aramaic: לְמִישְׁקַל עַפְרָא מִתּוּתֵי כַּרְעֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: to take dust from beneath the feet of Rabbi Chanina,
He said to her: Take it,
your plan will not succeed,
for it is written: 'There is none besides Him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי חנינא acting on his teaching from step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That כשפים have no power against ה׳.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the woman and the dust.

steps.title: But כשפים do have power
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects from רבי יוחנן, who says כשפים can weaken the Heavenly court.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוחנן said: Why is it called כשפים? Because they weaken the Heavenly court!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא using רבי יוחנן's explanation of the word כשפים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads כשפים as short for 'מכחישין פמליא של מעלה,' they weaken the Heavenly court. That means כשפים can work against what Heaven wants, which seems to contradict רבי חנינא.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying כשפים are stronger than ה׳. He means they can act against the normal Heavenly order, which is why the גמרא sees a contradiction.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
Why are they called 'keshafim'?
Because they weaken the Heavenly court!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי חנינא's teaching and story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's claim that כשפים have no power.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן says כשפים can act against the Heavenly court, so they do have power.

steps.title: רבי חנינא was different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי חנינא's great merit protected him from כשפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא is different, because his merit was great.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that כשפים usually do have power, but not against someone with as much merit as רבי חנינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So רבי יוחנן is right in general. רבי חנינא's confidence was special to him because of his great זכות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina is different, since his merit is great.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 27.
steps.terutzMaskana: כשפים usually have power, but not against someone with great זכות like רבי חנינא.

steps.title: Even a small injury is decreed in Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא teaches that a person does not even hurt his finger unless it was announced in Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חנינא said: A person does not hurt his finger below unless it is announced about him above, as it says: 'From ה׳ a man's steps are set, and what does a man understand of his way?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי חנינא about Heavenly control. Even the smallest injury comes from a Heavenly decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the idea that everything comes from ה׳. A פסוק shows that a person's steps are directed by ה׳, even when he does not understand why.

keyTerms.meaning: It is announced about him in Heaven

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chanina said:
A person does not hurt his finger below,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מַכְרִיזִין עָלָיו מִלְּמַעְלָה,
phrases.english: unless it is announced about him above,
as it says: 'From ה׳ a man's steps are set,'
phrases.notes: This mixes words from תהלים 37:23 and משלי 20:24.

phrases.english: 'and what does a man understand of his way?'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: אֵין אָדָם נוֹקֵף אֶצְבָּעוֹ מִלְּמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of רבי חנינא, also about ה׳ controlling everything.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every injury, even a small one, is decreed from Heaven.

steps.title: The blood of a small wound brings atonement
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that blood from a small wound brings כפרה like the blood of a קרבן עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The blood of a small wound brings atonement like the blood of an עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a related teaching about small injuries. רבי אלעזר says such a wound can bring כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the injury comes from Heaven, it has meaning. Its blood is compared to the blood of a קרבן עולה, which brings atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood from a small wound or bang

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
The blood of a wound brings atonement like the blood of a burnt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: דַּם נִיקּוּף מְרַצֶּה כְּדַם עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 29 about small injuries.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood from a small wound brings כפרה like an עולה.

steps.title: Which wound brings atonement
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits רבי אלעזר's teaching: a wound on the right thumb, a second wound, while going to do a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is about the right thumb, a second wound, and only when he is going to do a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains exactly which kind of wound רבי אלעזר meant. He adds three conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every scratch brings כפרה. It must be on the right thumb, be a second wound in the same place, and happen while going to do a מצוה.
steps.whatToRemember: A small injury comes from Heaven (רבי חנינא), and in certain cases its blood brings כפרה like an עולה (רבי אלעזר, as limited by רבא).

phrases.english: Rava said: On the right thumb,
and with a second wound,
and only when he is going to do a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבי אלעזר's teaching in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wound brings כפרה only on the right thumb, as a second wound, while going to a מצוה.

steps.title: רבי פנחס בן יאיר never benefited from others
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells that רבי פנחס בן יאיר never ate bread that was not his and never benefited even from his father's meals.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבי פנחס בן יאיר: He never broke bread on a piece that was not his, and from the time he was old enough to understand, he did not benefit from his father's meals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבי פנחס בן יאיר, discussed earlier on the דף, and describes how careful he was not to benefit from others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He never made a ברכה and ate bread that belonged to someone else. He even refused to benefit from his own father once he was grown up.

keyTerms.meaning: Broke bread and made a ברכה on a piece

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר:
phrases.english: They said about Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair:

phrases.aramaic: מִיָּמָיו לֹא בָּצַע עַל פְּרוּסָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ שֶׁלּוֹ,
phrases.english: In all his days he never broke bread on a piece that was not his,
and from the day he was old enough to understand,
he did not benefit from his father's meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי פנחס בן יאיר, who appeared earlier on the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי פנחס בן יאיר never benefited from anyone else, not even his father.
